purpose: Cyclobenzaprine is used to help relieve muscle spasms, stiffness, and pain caused by muscle injuries or strains. It is usually used along with rest and physical therapy to help your muscles heal. It is meant for short-term use, typically no longer than two to three weeks.
how_it_works: Cyclobenzaprine works in your brain and spinal cord to block the nerve signals that cause your muscles to tighten up and spasm. Think of it like a reset button that tells your overworked muscles to calm down and relax. It does not work directly on the muscle itself but rather through your nervous system.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are drowsiness, dry mouth, and dizziness. You may also feel tired, have blurred vision, feel a little confused, or have a headache. Some people also notice constipation or an upset stomach.
warnings: This medicine can make you very drowsy, so do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication because it can make the drowsiness much worse. Do not take it if you have recently used an MAO inhibitor antidepressant, or if you have heart problems, overactive thyroid, or certain other heart rhythm conditions. Tell your doctor about all your medications because this drug can interact with many others. It is not recommended for older adults as it can increase fall risk and confusion.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for adults is 5 mg taken three times a day. Your doctor may increase this to 10 mg three times a day if needed. The extended-release capsule version (Amrix) is typically taken once a day, usually 15 mg. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and do not use it for longer than two to three weeks.
